Let \(G=\mathbb F_\ell^r\) and \(Q=|G|=\ell^r\). The number is

\[
\boxed{
\ell^{r-2}\bigl(\ell^{r-1}-1\bigr)
+\mathbf 1_{\,r\mid(\ell-1)}(r-1)(\ell-1)(\ell-1-r)\ell^{r-3}\bigl(\ell^{r-2}-1\bigr)
}.
\]

Here \(\mathbf 1_{\,r\mid(\ell-1)}\) is \(1\) if \(r\mid \ell-1\), and \(0\) otherwise.

**Solution.**  
Write

\[
\sigma(\alpha_i^{(j)})=\zeta^{a_i^{(j)}}\alpha_{\pi(i)}^{(j)},\qquad
\sigma(\rho_j)=\zeta^{s_j}\rho_j .
\]

The relation \(\prod_i\alpha_i^{(j)}=\rho_{j+1}\) gives

\[
\sum_i a_i^{(j)}=s_{j+1}.
\]

Let the \(m=n/2=2q^2\) transposition blocks of \(\pi\) be \(T\), and define

\[
B_T=(a_i^{(1)}+a_{\pi(i)}^{(1)},\ldots,a_i^{(r)}+a_{\pi(i)}^{(r)})\in G.
\]

The multiset \(\{B_T\}\) has total sum

\[
\sum_T B_T=Ps.
\]

For fixed \(k\), \(\sigma\) acts on \(\Omega_k\) by

\[
(i,h,u)\mapsto
\left(\pi i,\pi h,\ u+ks+a_i-a_h\right),
\]

so \(\sigma^2\) fixes the ordered pair of transposition blocks and translates \(u\) by

\[
2ks+B_T-B_{T'}.
\]

Thus a \(2\)-cycle occurs exactly when this translation is zero. If

\[
N_x=\#\{T:B_T=x\},
\qquad
R(d)=\sum_x N_xN_{x-d},
\]

then the number \(C_k\) of \(2\)-cycles is

\[
C_k=
Q\bigl(2R(-2ks)-m\mathbf 1_{k=0}\bigr).
\]

Since every \(s_j\ne0\), the map \(k\mapsto -2ks\) is a bijection of \(G\). Therefore the given three-level condition on \(C_k\) is equivalent to

\[
R(d)=R_O
+4\ell(q+3Q)\mathbf 1_U(d)
+4\ell^2(q+Q)\mathbf 1_W(d)
+q^2\mathbf 1_{\{0\}}(d).
\]

Taking Fourier transforms on \(G\),

\[
|\widehat N(\chi)|=
\begin{cases}
2q^2,& \chi=0,\\
q+4Q,& \chi\in U^\perp\setminus\{0\},\\
q+2Q,& \chi\in W^\perp\setminus U^\perp,\\
q,& \chi\notin W^\perp.
\end{cases}
\]

Because \(2\) generates \(\mathbb F_\ell^\times\), the primes \(q,q+2Q,q+4Q\) are inert in \(\mathbb Q(\zeta)\). Also

\[
2q\equiv 1\pmod Q
\]

forces the root-of-unity signs in these Fourier coefficients to be positive. Fourier inversion then gives one conjugacy orbit for each admissible triple \((s,U,W)\), with the translation fixed by

\[
\sum_TB_T=Ps.
\]

So it remains only to count admissible \((s,U,W)\).

The condition

\[
\mathbf 1\in \operatorname{span}\{s,Ps\}
\]

means that for some \(A,B\in\mathbb F_\ell\),

\[
s_{j+1}=A+Bs_j
\]

cyclically. There are two cases.

If \(s\) is constant, then there are \(\ell-1\) choices. Here \(c_s=\mathbf 1\). The number of flags with \(\mathbf 1\in U\setminus W\) is

\[
\frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}\cdot \ell^{r-2}.
\]

This contributes

\[
(\ell-1)\frac{\ell^{r-1}-1}{\ell-1}\ell^{r-2}
=
\ell^{r-2}(\ell^{r-1}-1).
\]

If \(s\) is nonconstant, then \(B\) must have order \(r\), so this case exists only when \(r\mid \ell-1\). For each element \(B\) of order \(r\), the affine recurrence has

\[
(\ell-1)(\ell-1-r)
\]

solutions with all \(s_j\ne0\) and \(\mathbf 1\in\operatorname{span}\{s,Ps\}\). There are \(r-1\) such \(B\). In this case \(\mathbf 1\) and \(c_s\) are linearly independent. The number of flags with

\[
\mathbf 1,c_s\in U\setminus W
\]

is

\[
\frac{\ell^{r-2}-1}{\ell-1}\cdot \ell^{r-3}(\ell-1)
=
\ell^{r-3}(\ell^{r-2}-1).
\]

Thus the nonconstant contribution is

\[
\mathbf 1_{\,r\mid(\ell-1)}
(r-1)(\ell-1)(\ell-1-r)
\ell^{r-3}(\ell^{r-2}-1).
\]

Adding the two contributions gives the boxed formula.
